item.title: Sajek shutdown puts Tk20cr in tourism business at risk
item.description:
All tourists have left Sajek Valley in Rangamati’s Baghaichhari upazila amid security concerns, leaving the popular hill destination deserted as local tourism businesses brace for potential losses of around Tk20 crore during a 10-day closure coinciding with the Durga Puja holidays.
Around 1,000 tourists were escorted to Khagrachhari in two groups at 10:30am and 2:30pm on Monday under the protection of law enforcement agencies. No tourists are currently staying at Sajek, and new visitors are being barred from entering the area.
The temporary closure has raised concerns among tourism entrepreneurs, who had expected a surge in visitors during the Durga Puja holidays and the upcoming winter tourism season. They said most resorts and cottages had advance bookings for October 16-25, making the shutdown a major financial blow at a crucial time of the year.
On Sunday, Rangamati Deputy Commissioner Nazma Ashrafi issued an emergency public notice announcing the temporary closure of Sajek Valley in view of the overall security situation. The notice instructed all tourists staying there to leave by 5pm on Monday.
According to the Sajek Cottage and Resort Owners Association, all tourists were safely evacuated in two groups before the deadline, under the supervision of law enforcement agencies.
Earlier on Sunday, the Sajek Gonodhikar Rokkha Committee and the Sajek Karbari Association enforced a road blockade from 6am to 5pm, disrupting traffic on the Sajek road and leaving tourists stranded.
The protesters agreed to suspend the blockade for two days following lengthy discussions with law enforcement agencies on Sunday afternoon. Authorities subsequently began escorting stranded tourists to Khagrachhari under heightened security.
With Durga Puja beginning on October 16, tourism businesses had anticipated a significant influx of visitors, particularly between October 20 and 24. The approaching winter season had also raised expectations of a strong recovery in business.
Yothen Tripura, owner of Megh Samudra Resort in Sajek, said around 90% of the resort’s rooms had been booked for October 16-25.
“The sudden decision to close Sajek has pushed us towards major financial losses. Many tourists have already cancelled their bookings after hearing about the closure, and we have to refund their money,” he said.
Calling the period crucial for the industry, he urged the administration to assess the situation and allow tourism businesses to resume operations once adequate security could be ensured.
Mohammad Jasim Uddin, a Mahindra driver operating on the Khagrachhari-Sajek route, said the closure had also hit transport workers.
“My three trips have been cancelled over the past three days, including on Tuesday. When there are no tourists, our income stops,” he said.
Rahul Chakma Jan, organising secretary of the Sajek Cottage and Resort Owners Association, said all tourists had left the area before the administration’s deadline and no new visitors were being allowed to enter.
He said tourist arrivals remained relatively low during much of the year, while weekly holidays, Eid, Durga Puja and the winter season brought the largest crowds. Businesses rely on earnings during these peak periods to offset losses during the rest of the year.
According to Rahul, Sajek has around 130-135 resorts, 20-25 restaurants and numerous other tourism-related businesses. Vehicle owners and drivers transporting tourists from Khagrachhari also depend on the sector for their livelihoods.
He estimated that tourism businesses in Sajek generate around Tk2 crore a day during peak periods. A 10-day closure from October 16 to 25 could therefore result in losses of approximately Tk20 crore.
The fallout could extend well beyond resort and cottage owners, affecting restaurant operators, transport workers, tour guides, employees and small traders, tourism stakeholders said.
Many local families depend on tourism for their livelihoods, and a prolonged shutdown could further strain their household incomes.
Tourism entrepreneurs have urged the administration to reopen Sajek Valley as soon as the security situation permits. They hope that restoring access ahead of Durga Puja and the winter season will help avert some of the anticipated losses.

item.title: Two killed as under-construction roof collapses in Rangpur
item.description:
Two workers were killed and seven others injured after the roof shuttering of an under-construction municipal building collapsed in Pirganj upazila of Rangpur on Tuesday afternoon.
The deceased were identified as Asadul Haque, a resident of Sadullapur upazila in Gaibandha, and Shihab from Rangpur.
The accident occurred at the under-construction building of Pirganj Municipality in Arajigangarampur area of the upazila. Contractors from Vision 2020 were reportedly carrying out the construction work.
Locals said 13 workers had been working on the roof of the building since morning when the shuttering suddenly collapsed, trapping four workers under the debris.
A team from Pirganj Fire Service rushed to the scene and rescued the trapped workers, who were taken to the hospital in critical condition. Later, doctors on duty declared Asadul and Shihab dead.
Local residents also rescued five injured workers and took them to Pirganj Upazila Health Complex. Three of the injured were identified as Liton Mandal, Salim Mia and Babla Mia. The identities of the other injured workers were not immediately known.
Pirganj Fire Service Station Officer Nazmul Sarkar said two of the injured are receiving treatment in critical condition.
Rangpur-6 lawmaker Nurul Amin visited the scene and demanded that those responsible for any negligence be brought to justice.

item.title: Fire breaks out at Essential Drug International in Tongi, 13 units deployed
item.description:
A fire broke out at Essential Drug International in the Cherag Ali area of Tongi in Gazipur this morning (Wednesday).

The Fire Service and Civil Defence (FSCD) received the information t of the fire at 10:15 am and immediately dispatched firefighting units to the spot.

The first units reached the scene at 10:25am, about two kilometres from Tongi Fire Station, FSCD media officer Talha bin Zasim told BSS over phone call.

Eight firefighting units are currently working to bring the blaze under control, while five more units are on their way, taking the total number of deployed units to 13, he said.

The cause of the fire and the extent of damage, as well as any possible casualties, have yet to be ascertained.

Firefighting operations are underway.

item.title: Govt approves LNG purchases from 5 international suppliers
item.description:
Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has recommended in-principle approval for proposals to procure liquefied natural gas (LNG) from five international suppliers to maintain the country's gas supply and meet emergency energy needs.

The recommendations came at the committee's 33rd meeting of 2026, held virtually yesterday, Tuesday (on 13 October) with Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury in the chair where two proposals from the Energy and Mineral Resources Division were presented and discussed.

The first proposal sought in-principle approval to process LNG supply proposals submitted by Cheniere Marketing International LLP and Trafigura Pte Ltd under the government-to-government (G2G) method.

The proposal cited Section 68 of the Public Procurement Act, 2006, and Rules 99(2) and 107(2) of the Public Procurement Rules, 2025.

The second proposal sought in-principle approval to purchase LNG directly from BP Singapore Pte. Limited, Sahara Energy Resource Limited and Shell International Trading Middle East Limited FZE to maintain an uninterrupted gas supply in the country in the interest of public welfare and to meet urgent national requirements.

The proposal cited Section 68 of the Public Procurement Act, 2006, and Rules 97, 98 and 107 of the Public Procurement Rules, 2025.

Both proposals came from the Energy and Mineral Resources Division.

item.title: Nobel Prize pays tribute to historic 114-year-old Tagore-Russel correspondence
item.description:
The official social media platforms of the Nobel Prize have shared a rare, 114-year-old handwritten letter exchanged between literature laureates Rabindranath Tagore and Bertrand Russell, highlighting a historic intersection of Eastern philosophy and Western thought.

The Nobel Prize showcased the artifact with the caption, “Take a look at this 114-year-old correspondence between literature laureates Bertrand Russell and Rabindranath Tagore,” drawing immense global attention to the rare document preserved in the Bertrand Russell Archives at McMaster University Library in Canada.

The correspondence, penned by Tagore on 13 October 1912, reveals that the legendary Indian poet had just finished reading Russell’s analytical article titled “The Essence of Religion,” which was published in the Hibbert Journal.

Tagore wrote to the British philosopher that the piece deeply resonated with him, stating that the discourse reminded him of a sacred verse from the Upanishads—the ancient Sanskrit texts that form the core foundations for many Hindu traditions.

The two 20th-century intellectual giants had met personally when Tagore visited England earlier that year in 1912, setting off a profound cross-cultural philosophical friendship.

In the letter, Tagore seamlessly bridges their shared concepts of ego-transcendence by transcribing the classical Sanskrit verse directly into the text, followed by a detailed English translation and commentary on how the “Infinite self” overcomes the limitations of the “finite self” to live a life free of fear.

This monumental exchange took place at a major turning point in global literary history. Almost a year after writing this letter, Rabindranath Tagore achieved the historic milestone of becoming the first non-European to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for his poetry. Bertrand Russell would later follow in his footsteps, receiving the same prestigious global honor 37 years later in 1950.

Cultural historians and literary archivists view the Nobel Committee’s global feature of this epistle as a timely reminder of a golden era of philosophy, showing how ancient Vedic insights and modern Western rationale harmoniously converged to address the universal human condition.

item.title: Youth Development Department to hold exam despite question paper leak
item.description:
The Department of Youth Development is set to hold the postponed examination for the post of Assistant Upazila Youth Development Officer next Friday, retaining the existing recruitment committee despite the question paper leak.

Several officials at the Ministry of Youth and Sports and at least one member of the committee believe it should be reconstituted to restore candidates’ confidence.

The department had scheduled the preliminary screening examination for the post at 98 centres across Dhaka on Saturday. Around 319,000 candidates applied for 242 positions.

The department postponed the examination shortly before it was due to begin after finding that the original question paper matched one that had circulated on social media.

The department has rescheduled the postponed examination for Friday, 16 October, from 3:00 pm to 4:00 pm. The Ministry of Youth and Sports also formed a five-member committee, headed by Additional Secretary Mahfuzul Alam Khan, to investigate the question paper leak.

The committee was due to submit its report yesterday, Tuesday, but has requested two additional days.

Mahfuzul Alam Khan, chairman of the investigation committee, told Prothom Alo that he had sought an extension of two days because some investigative work remained outstanding. “We have collected all the information and evidence. We are now verifying them. A technology expert from the Information and Technology Division has been included in the committee. We have taken statements from all members involved in preparing the question paper,” he said.

New date announced for cancelled Department of Youth Development recruitment test

Several officials at the Ministry of Youth and Sports said the recruitment committee could not evade responsibility for the question paper leak.

One committee member also told Prothom Alo that reconstituting the committee would have sent a positive message to candidates.

A source familiar with the matter said some committee members had requested to step down, but the authorities did not consider their requests.

Asked about the matter, Department of Youth Development Director General Motaher Hossain told Prothom Alo on Tuesday night that the identities of those involved in the question paper leak remained unknown.

“Therefore, the committee cannot be held responsible. Besides, the Department of Youth Development does not have the authority to form a new committee. The Ministry of Youth and Sports can do so after seeking the opinion of the Ministry of Public Administration. That has not been done,” he said.

He added, “Under the arrangements for the rescheduled examination, the departmental promotion committee (DPC) has no scope to take any action.”

Attempts to contact Youth and Sports Ministry Secretary Md Mahbub-ul-Alam by mobile phone for his comments were unsuccessful.

The correspondent also tried to contact State Minister for Youth and Sports Md Aminul Haque by phone and subsequently sent him a text message, but no response was received.

A five-member departmental recruitment committee (DPC) oversees recruitment to the post of Assistant Upazila Youth Development Officer.

Joint Secretary of the Department of Youth Development DM Atikur Rahman, who serves as director of its administration and finance division, chairs the committee. Deputy Director (Administration) of the department Atikur Rahman serves as its member-secretary.

The other three members are Mizanur Rahman, a deputy secretary at the Ministry of Youth and Sports; a member of the Bangladesh Public Service Commission (BPSC); and a representative of the Ministry of Public Administration.

According to sources at the Department of Youth Development, the authorities have changed the location for preparing and printing the question papers for the 16 October examination.

The question papers will be prepared and printed in the meeting room of the Ministry of Youth and Sports at the Secretariat on the night before the examination. For the previous examination, officials prepared and printed the question papers at the department’s office in Motijheel.

Abdul Awal Majumder, a former secretary and former rector of the Bangladesh Public Administration Training Centre (BPATC), told Prothom Alo that the government could have reconstituted the recruitment committee if it had wanted to.

“The current recruitment committee will surely remain cautious following the question paper leak. They will not want any new controversy to arise,” he said.

item.title: Top Indian ‘cockroach’ leaders sent to jail over trespassing: Party
item.description:

Two top leaders of India’s youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) were sent to jail for five days on Wednesday for alleged trespassing, the party said.

Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das “have been sent to five days judicial custody”, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said in a social media post.

Das and Ranka were detained on Tuesday for entering Jantar Mantar, a day after Delhi Police announced that the Jantar Mantar street in the heart of the capital had been taken off the list of designated official protest sites.

A video posted online by Dipke on Tuesday showed the duo clambering over barricades at Jantar Mantar street, running into an empty space and waving the national flag -- before police chased and detained them.

Supporters of the online movement and opposition parties have taken to the streets in recent days, demanding the resignation of the head of India’s election commission, accusing it of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party.

The Election Commission of India, which oversees the voting process in the world’s most populous nation, has denied any wrongdoing.

The site has been sealed off for several days by yellow metal barricades and guarded by a heavy police presence.

Dipke on Wednesday defended Das and Ranka, saying they were being punished just for “unfurling tricolour at Jantar Mantar.

“Show some guts, @narendramodi,” he said.

item.title: Saudi says Houthi attacks sparked Aramco fire, wounded 4 in Riyadh
item.description:
Saudi Arabia said on Wednesday that an attack on an Aramco building in the kingdom’s east sparked a “limited fire” and that debris from intercepted Houthi missiles wounded four people in the capital Riyadh.

It came hours after the Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen’s Houthis said it had intercepted several missiles on Tuesday evening, including over Riyadh.

A Saudi energy ministry official said an administrative building belonging to oil giant Aramco in Dhahran was struck on Tuesday evening, resulting in a “limited fire” but “no casualties or fatalities”.

Saudi Arabia’s civil defence agency said on Wednesday that four people -- two women, a man and a child -- were wounded by debris from two intercepted Houthi cruise missiles in the capital and that 15 homes were damaged.

Earlier on Tuesday, the coalition struck oil sites across western Yemen, in response to the deadliest attack on the kingdom’s soil in years.

The strikes in Yemen’s Sanaa and the western provinces of Dhamar and Saada targeted facilities used to “supply the war effort” by the Houthis to “threaten the kingdom, Yemen, the southern Red Sea and waterways”, coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki wrote on X.

A powerful explosion then rang out in the Saudi capital, with a phone alert sent to residents saying “the city of Riyadh is facing a hostile aerial threat”.

While walking down a major avenue in Riyadh, a witness told AFP he “saw a projectile cutting across the sky” above a mall, saying it left “a yellowish trail of light followed by a trail of smoke. Then, we heard an explosion”.

“People were calm; no one was speaking. We were scared and all looking up at the sky,” he added, requesting anonymity.

After Houthi strikes on Saudi airports and energy sites in recent days, the coalition issued its first evacuation order in the Yemeni capital since the war flared in July, before attacking the Yemen Petroleum Company facility on Sanaa’s outskirts.

An AFP correspondent in Sanaa reported an explosion, while a breaking news alert on the Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah TV channel said “Saudi aggression” targeted the oil firm.

Renewed threats

 A strike on Riyadh’s international airport on Saturday left 13 people dead and operations suspended in the worst attack since 2015.

The Saudi cabinet vowed in a meeting earlier Tuesday, led by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, that it “will not allow its security or freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait to be threatened”.

An AFP correspondent reported that many civilians in Sanaa, fearing shortages, rushed to queue in front of fuel stations after the coalition warning.

The Houthis had earlier issued a new threat to target Riyadh’s international airport, a refinery, and an Aramco facility in Dammam if the strike went ahead, calling for citizens to avoid them.

Many countries have issued travel warnings to their citizens in Saudi Arabia, most recently France, which told its citizens to avoid Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam airports.

The Saudi-led coalition has supported Yemen’s government militarily against the Houthis since 2015 in a long-running civil war that has created a dire humanitarian crisis.

Economic woes

 Traffic in perennially gridlocked Riyadh was noticeably lighter this week as remote learning for all schools and work-from-home orders for some companies took effect, according to AFP journalists.

Saudi Arabia faces a major economic contraction this year, with GDP expected to shrink 3.3 per cent, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday, predicting a regional drop over Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

The kingdom was already facing headwinds from Iran’s chokehold on the Hormuz strait since the start of the Middle East war in February, when the US and Israel attacked Iran.

But the restart in July of Yemen’s frozen war has further roiled the kingdom and brought the fight to its own soil.

Houthi attacks have also targeted oil tankers in the Red Sea -- Saudi Arabia’s alternative export route.

In Yemen, the renewed fighting was fuelling the risk of infectious disease outbreaks.

Suspected cholera cases tripled there in three weeks, the World Health Organization said Tuesday, warning that the growing disease burden was straining hospitals already treating war casualties.

‘Behaving very badly’

 The Riyadh airport attack had prompted US President Donald Trump to say he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis.

He wrote on his Truth Social platform on Tuesday that “the Houthis are behaving very badly”, accusing them of acting “probably at the behest of Iran”.

“I’ll be there after the elections, and I will never forget!” he wrote, referring to next month’s midterms.

The Houthis warned the US against intervention, with political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti telling AFP they would target American interests in the region.

Bukhaiti said the purpose of the campaign against Saudi targets was to send a message to the crown prince “that he can no longer wage aggression against Yemen from a safe position”.

Man and wife allegedly led temple gold theft ring
item.description:
A man and his wife allegedly travelled from one temple to another in Dhaka to steal gold ornaments from idols. Police identified the couple while investigating the theft of gold placed on the tongue of the idol of Goddess Kali at Ramna Kali Mandir (temple) in the capital city.

Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Joint Commissioner (Crime) Faruk Hossain disclosed the information at a press conference at the DMP Media Centre on Minto Road in the capital on Tuesday afternoon.

Faruk Hossain said investigators had found evidence linking Arnab Roy and his wife, Lipi Karmakar, to gold thefts at two other temples besides Ramna Kali Temple. Two other people, both gold shop owners, have also been arrested in connection with the cases.

Identified through CCTV footage, gold recovered

The theft at Ramna Kali Mandir at Shahbagh took place between 8:45 am and 4:00 pm on 7 October, the police official said. Gold weighing approximately six annas was stolen from the tongue of the idol of Goddess Kali. The gold was estimated to be worth Tk 80,000. Temple priest Sujit Chakraborty filed a complaint with Shahbagh police station.

Police examined CCTV footage from the temple and used information technology to identify those involved. They subsequently arrested Arnab Roy and Lipi Karmakar from the Dobadia area under Uttarkhan police station. A case was filed with Shahbagh police station. After their arrest, the two were produced before a court, where they gave confessional statements.

Based on information provided by the couple, police arrested Md Muhin, owner of Sadia Jewellers in the Dakkhin Khan area. A gold sheet weighing two annas and one ratti was recovered from him. Police said it was part of the gold stolen from Ramna Kali Temple.

Linked to Siddheshwari temple theft

Gold ornaments were stolen from Siddheshwari Kali Temple on 13 September, and a case was filed with Ramna police station. During questioning, police obtained information linking the couple to the theft. The stolen ornaments were subsequently recovered based on information they provided.

The couple had sold the ornaments to a jewellery shop owner named Zakaria Islam, who has also been arrested.

DMP Joint Commissioner Faruk Hossain said Arnab Roy was also accused of attempting to steal a gold chain from an idol of Baba Lokenath Brahmachari at a temple in Deobhog, Narayanganj, on 11 September. A temple priest caught him while he was fleeing with the chain. Members of the temple committee later released him.

Faruk Hossain told Prothom Alo that, based on the information gathered so far, police had linked Arnab Roy and Lipi Karmakar to three incidents. The couple allegedly visited different temples to steal gold ornaments.

Police are investigating whether they were involved in similar thefts beyond these three cases and whether others were part of the alleged ring, he added.

item.title: ‘No More Silence’ publishes identities of people making obscene comments
item.description:
“What would you do if all men disappeared from the world for 24 hours?” In response to this question, a young woman said, “I would walk alone at night. I’d walk around at 3:00am and see what it feels like.”

The young woman’s response in an interview that went viral on social media last year reflected women’s desire to move around freely and safely. Yet, instead of discussing women’s safety, they are often blamed themselves.

A 15-year-old girl who recently died in a paddy field in Lalmai, Cumilla, was not spared such victim-blaming either. Her rape and murder should have prompted a discussion about women’s safety. Instead, some people on social media have been posting obscene comments and mocking the girl herself.

A Facebook group called ‘No More Silence’ has taken a different approach to counter such comments. The group publishes photographs, identities and links to the Facebook profiles of people who post obscene comments about women under news reports and posts about widely discussed incidents.

How the group started

As soon as one visits the Facebook group, one sees photographs, identities and links to the profiles of people who made obscene comments about the girl from Cumilla. Some of them live abroad, while others are physicians, employees or students. The list includes men of different ages. Some of their comments are so obscene that they cannot be reproduced.

The group was launched on 2 November last year, nearly a year ago. It now has more than 30,000 members.

The group claims to have exposed the identities of more than 100 people who made offensive comments about women. In several cases, screenshots of the comments were sent to the individuals’ workplaces, educational institutions and embassies. According to the group, some of the individuals were subsequently warned by their employers or educational institutions.

The group’s founder, Abir Ahmed, is a writer and online activist. He told Prothom Alo that ‘No More Silence’ is a Facebook group dedicated to raising social awareness. Its purpose is to bring public attention to instances in which people’s dignity is undermined through derogatory, insulting and hateful comments on social media.

One of the group’s two moderators is Umme Suraiya, who has completed a master’s degree in political science. The other moderator, Zakia Hossain, is a second-year higher secondary student.

The group was formed following an incident of sexual harassment of women at a concert in Habiganj. The concert was organised at Jalal Stadium in Habiganj to mark the silver jubilee of the Management Department of Brindaban Government College. Disorder broke out at the event, and news outlets reported that women attending the concert had faced sexual harassment and molestation.

Amid the reports, a Facebook account described in vulgar language an incident in which a woman had been touched inappropriately. The post received ‘ha ha’ reactions. Angered by what they saw, Abir Ahmed and his two associates decided to set up the group.

Exposing the identities of ‘offenders’

On 30 September, a television channel published a news card about the recovery of a woman’s body with her throat slit in a hotel bathroom in Cox’s Bazar. The woman had filed a case against her husband over a family dispute. She had checked into a hotel in Cox’s Bazar to attend a hearing in the case, accompanied by her two-and-a-half-year-old child and a man. Her body was later found in the hotel bathroom. The child was in the room, while the man had fled.

‘No More Silence’ published the photographs and identities of six people who made obscene comments under the news card about the incident.

On 15 January, a television channel reported allegations that several people, including a bus driver and his assistant, had gang-raped a passenger inside a bus in Savar. The group published the photographs and identities of five people who posted comments supporting rape under the report.

According to the group, police detained a young man from Faridpur after it posted about him making videos of himself behaving inappropriately with his own sister. The young man later appeared on Facebook to apologise and pledged not to make such videos again.

Need to raise awareness

While the initiative seeks to establish social accountability for obscene comments, publishing people’s identities also carries the risk of misidentification.

After the mother of the girl from Cumilla spoke publicly demanding justice for her daughter’s murder, a man posted an obscene comment under a news report about her statement. He identified himself as a sales employee at the Bishwo Rang showroom in Sunrise Plaza in the capital. However, after the group published his identity, Bishwo Rang issued a statement saying it had no employee by that name.

The incident highlights the importance of verifying information before exposing someone’s identity online. If someone makes a comment using a fake account in another person’s name, publishing that person’s identity without confirming who is behind the account could lead to an innocent individual being harassed.

The law provides for punishment for obscene comments targeting women, sexual harassment, and the creation and distribution of sexually abusive material by manipulating women’s images. Section 25 of the Cyber Security Act 2026 provides for punishment for publishing harmful or intimidating material through digital platforms for the purposes of blackmail, sexual harassment, revenge pornography, digital child sexual abuse material or sextortion.

Manisha Biswas, focal person for the Cyber Support for Women and Children (CSWC) platform of the Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (BLAST), told Prothom Alo that women rarely seek legal remedies over offensive comments and image manipulation. This emboldens those responsible for such offences.

Social media has become a space where even insulting comments can attract more likes and comments, she said. People need to be held accountable for what they post, and public awareness should be raised by informing people about the penalties prescribed by law.

However, Biswas advised caution when publishing the identities of people accused of wrongdoing. She said it was essential to verify whether someone else might be posting comments using a fake account in another person’s name before disclosing their identity.

item.title: Rivers and geopolitics: Is Teesta project turning into a geopolitical game?
item.description:
• While discussions were ongoing about the technical issues of the Power-China Teesta project, the geopolitical tension between India and China regarding this project became apparent.

  • Given the Bangladesh-US trade agreement and the nearly Tk 120 billion budget of this project, it wouldn't be surprising if the US shows interest.

Bangladesh has already faced geopolitical tensions between India and China over the Teesta barrage project. Recently, some interest from the US has also become visible regarding this project. In a two-part series, Nazrul Islam writes about how the Teesta Barrage Project has turned into a geopolitical game and how its detrimental effects can be avoided. The first part was published today.

US Ambassador to Bangladesh, Brent T Christensen, along with his wife, visited the Teesta barrage project sites in Lalmonirhat and Nilphamari on 30 August. Senior economic and political officials from the US Embassy in Dhaka were also part of this delegation. The US Ambassador's visit to the remote Teesta area naturally sparked curiosity among people.

Ambassador Christensen's visit was not limited to the Teesta Barrage; he also visited various economic institutions in the area, including Paragon Dairy of Paragon Group in Gangachara upazila of Rangpur, Green Field Tea Industries Limited in Panchagarh, and the country's largest central railway workshop in Parbatipur.

Visit to the Teesta and the recent Bangladesh-US trade agreement

Many experts see a connection between the recent (9 February 2026) trade agreement signed between Bangladesh and the US and the visit by the US Ambassador and senior officials to the Teesta area. A common goal of this widely discussed agreement is to expand the market for American companies within Bangladesh. Among these, dairy products are specifically mentioned.

However, this market is not limited to goods alone; it also applies to various types of services. One of these is construction contracting. The contract work for large-budget projects implemented with government funding is particularly attractive. This trade agreement emphasises, directly or indirectly, that American companies should also be able to secure such work.

Naturally, the Teesta project comes up in this context. Given the Bangladesh-US trade agreement and the nearly Tk 120 billion budget of this project, it wouldn't be surprising if the US shows interest. But Bangladesh has already encountered geopolitical tensions between India and China over the Teesta project. The involvement of the US would undoubtedly complicate the situation further. The question is, how will Bangladesh manage this complex situation?

The Teesta river, barrage, and crisis

To understand the issue, one must first know some facts about the Teesta River and the project. The Teesta is Bangladesh's fourth-largest river, originating in the Indian state of Sikkim at the foothills of the Himalayas, flowing through West Bengal before entering Bangladesh, and finally merging with the Jamuna near Chilmari in Kurigram. Being close to the Himalayas, this river is swift (with a steep slope), prone to flash floods, seasonal, and carries sediment. Sediment-laden, seasonal rivers are generally braided because, during low-flow seasons, sediment deposition causes sandbars and the river divides into multiple channels around these bars. As a result, braided rivers become wider than their flow.

For a commercial approach to rivers, India constructed multiple dams on the Teesta and its tributaries in Sikkim to harness hydropower potential. Meanwhile, Bangladesh's water authorities saw irrigation potential in the Teesta and considered building a barrage to implement it. Indian authorities were also interested in using Teesta's water to expand irrigation in West Bengal and completed the Gajoldoba barrage by 1987. Although Bangladesh started the barrage idea before India, it fell behind in implementation and completed the barrage at Dalia in 1990.

However, building a barrage at Dalia without any agreement or assurance on how much flow would be available from Teesta during the dry season doesn't turn out to be a wise decision for Bangladesh since India, taking advantage of its upstream position, gradually increases the irrigated area and the amount of water withdrawn from Teesta. As a result, the purpose of the Dalia barrage gets largely thwarted and instead becomes a problem for Bangladesh.

Firstly, during the dry season, there's not enough water in the river for irrigation. Secondly, if the little water reaching the Dalia barrage is diverted, there's no water left in the main part of the Teesta from Dalia to Chilmari, a stretch of 102 kilometers in Bangladesh. Thirdly, during the monsoon season and flash floods, India opens all the gates of the Gajoldoba barrage to avoid potential flooding, and Bangladesh does the same at the Dalia barrage to prevent flooding upstream.

At that time, a huge volume of water rushes downstream, causing floods. Fourthly, another problem arises. During the dry season, due to the riverbed drying up in Bangladesh, many sandbars form, the river becomes shallow, and it can't contain monsoon waters; instead, the riverbanks, laden with stones and sand, erode and widen. As a result, the width of the Teesta has increased by about threefold to around 3.1 kilometers.

Thousands of families have been rendered destitute, becoming refugees in Dhaka's slums or starting anew on sandbars.

The various issues with Power-China's Teesta project

It was the responsibility of Bangladesh's water authorities to find and implement solutions to the human-made crisis of the Teesta. However, they didn't show that capability and instead sought external assistance. This led to the emergence of a project by the Power-China company regarding the Teesta. Power-China arranged for a loan of about one billion dollars on commercial terms from China's Exim Bank for this project.

There's no doubt that China is now the most advanced country in various technological fields, especially in constructing bridges, dams, and barrages over rivers. However, the character of Bangladeshi rivers is very different from that of Chinese rivers. Therefore, understanding the uniqueness of the Teesta River and deriving an effective solution based on that is difficult even for Chinese experts. Initially (according to the 2019 feasibility study), the main features of their proposed project were as follows:

1. Denying Teesta's braided character and transforming it into a single-channel (meandering) river;

2. Reducing the average width of the river from the current nearly 3 kilometers to 816 meters (700 meters from Dalia to Kaunia and 1 kilometer from Kaunia to Chilmari);

3. Increasing the average depth of the river from 5 meters to 10 meters through dredging;

4. Using dredged materials to fill the river bed area and use it for urbanisation, industrialisation, etc. ;

5. Constructing embankments on both sides of the entire Teesta from Dalia to Chilmari to confine the monsoon flow within an 816-meter-wide channel;

6. As part of this process, effectively disconnecting Teesta from all its branches and tributaries by constructing embankments on their banks.

From BAPA (Bangladesh Paribesh Andolon), BEN (Bangladesh Environmental Network), and the Teesta Protection Movement, both I and Professor Khalequzzaman from the University of Pennsylvania in the US closely reviewed the Power-China project design and showed that it's impractical for various reasons.

Firstly, a braided river by natural causes can't be forcibly transformed into a single-channel river; even if all engineering might is used to do that, this unnatural transformation won't be sustainable, and the river will soon revert to its original braided character.

Secondly, the narrow embankments constructed on the river's banks and shores will be prone to erosion, and cities and industries built outside the embankments will be flooded.

Thirdly, the nearly 40 million tonnes of sediment carried annually through the Teesta River will accumulate at the bottom, soon negating any increase in depth achieved through dredging, further reducing the river's monsoon water-holding capacity. Overall, the entire Power-China project will fail, and Teesta's problems will become more complex. (For a more detailed discussion of these issues, see the document titled 'Teesta River in Crisis: Which Way to a Solution'.

Bangladesh's water authorities were annoyed by our criticism because they wanted the project approved and proceeded with its implementation as quickly as possible. They didn't seem too concerned about whether the project would truly solve the Teesta issue. Some residents of the Teesta area were also unhappy, feeling that we were becoming obstacles on the path to solving the Teesta problem.

Of course, we can't really blame them for that, because the government had maintained extreme secrecy regarding the Teesta project. As a result, they had no clear understanding of the detailed design of the project and couldn't arrive at well-considered decisions about its accuracy.

However, it seems that it was impossible for Chinese experts to ignore our analysis. Consequently, they presented a revised project design in 2023. This design maintained the goal of transforming the Teesta from a braided river to a single-channel river and reducing its average width to 816 meters, but introduced significant changes in some areas.

Firstly, instead of constructing embankments parallel to the riverbed, it was proposed to build them at an average distance of about one kilometer from the riverbed (the average distance between embankments on both banks is 2.8 kilometers).

Secondly, instead of increasing the river's depth to 10 meters through dredging, a complex profile was proposed for the river's bed. These changes introduced new issues, such as how urbanisation and industrialisation would be possible if embankments were constructed an average of one kilometer away from the riverbed and if the area within the embankments was subject to biannual flooding. How would they be protected from bank erosion if the river bed width remains at 816 meters?

Thirdly, how would the design of the river bed with narrow, steep gorges survive against the flow of about 40 million tonnes of sand and sediment annually? At a meeting held at the Water Development Board office on 17 July 2025, BAPA, BEN, and the Teesta Protection Movement raised these questions about the revised Power-China project. Power-China couldn't provide satisfactory answers.

India-China tension over the Teesta project

While discussions on the technical issues of Power-China's Teesta project were ongoing, the geopolitical tension between India and China regarding the project came to light. According to various sources, India felt uneasy about this Chinese project being so close to its narrow passageway to its seven northeastern states and proposed to Bangladesh to implement and finance the project itself.

This proposal from India put the then-Awami League government in a quandary; although the government had turned to China precisely because it hadn't received a positive response from India on the Teesta agreement, it was difficult to ignore India's proposal.

This change in stance by the then-Prime Minister angered China, which they communicated during her visit in 2024. Thus, the Teesta Project became a geopolitical issue. The US ’s entry into this project would undoubtedly make the situation more complicated. Now the question is, how can Bangladesh solve the Teesta problem and avoid the harmful effects of geopolitics?

* Nazrul Islam is a professor at the Asian Growth Research Institute and former head of development research at the United Nations.

* The opinions expressed here are the author's own.

* This article, originally published in Prothom Alo print and online editions, has been rewritten in English by Rabiul Islam

item.title: Young man detained over Dhaka footpath assault, inactive cop withdrawn
item.description:
Police arrested Khalid Hasan, 35, who was seen assaulting a man on a footpath in Dhaka’s Dhanmondi, near Meena Bazar in the area at around 11:45am on Wednesday.

Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) Abdul Hai of Dhanmondi Police Station, who was present at the scene during the assault, has been withdrawn from his post over allegations of negligence of duty.

Muhammad Imdadul Islam Tayeb, officer-in-charge (OC) of Dhanmondi Police Station, told Prothom Alo at noon that Khalid had been arrested over allegations of assaulting Shahid Abdullah Al Masud, also known as Masud Rana (48) and forcing him to do sit-ups while holding his ears.

The incident took place around noon on Monday opposite Bangladesh Eye Hospital on Satmasjid Road.

Khalid was produced before the court of the Special Metropolitan Magistrate under the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Ramna zone on Wednesday. OC Imdadul Islam said Shahid Abdullah suffers from a mental illness.

On Monday afternoon, Shahid Abdullah was accused of sexually harassing a 23 year old woman. Following the allegation, Khalid was seen slapping, kicking and forcing him to do sit ups while holding his ears.

A video of the incident later spread on social media, triggering widespread discussion and criticism. The assault, however, became the central focus of the debate.

Police said Khalid, who was arrested in connection with the incident, works as a graphic designer at a private company.

The woman told Prothom Alo on Wednesday that Shahid Abdullah had touched her inappropriately. She alleged that police officers present at the scene were reluctant to detain him. She then called a relative over the phone, who arrived and then beat Shahid Abdullah.

She said that her relative is now facing harassment for coming to her defence, having been detained by police and forwarded to the magistrate court, while the police officers who stood by silently during the incident faced little accountability. She questioned what steps were being taken against those officers.

The woman said she went to Dhanmondi Police Station on Wednesday morning after learning of her relative’s detention. According to her, police told her that the incident would not have happened if the video had not gone viral on social media.

She said she would file a case against the person who uploaded the video that went viral and demanded her relative’s release.

Asked what action had been taken against the police officers present at the scene, OC Imdadul Islam told Prothom Alo that ASI Abdul Hai had been withdrawn from the police station.

Hai had been on duty at the scene, he said. The other two officers present belonged to the Public Order Management unit, which handles riot control and he had no information about any action against them.

A 2 minute and 12 second video circulated on social media shows a young man angrily hurling abuse at Shahid Abdullah while slapping and kicking him. Pedestrians crowded around the spot, with some watching and others recording the incident on their mobile phones.

Some conversations among the bystanders can be heard in the video. Some are heard saying, “He touched the woman,” “This happened in the canteen,” and “Doesn’t he have a mother or sister?”

At one point, a passer-by approaches the man being assaulted and points towards two police officers at the scene, telling the others to hand the man over to them.

The man being assaulted is then seen getting up from a seated position. A bystander and the young man assaulting him take his mobile phone and question him about various matters.

The agitated young man is heard saying, “What sorry? Does saying sorry make everything alright?" He then slaps the man again, shouting, "...You laid hands on a mother."

The video shows two police officers standing just a few feet away as the incident unfolds on the footpath. Like the bystanders gathered around them, the officers appear to be watching the incident.

Many people on Facebook have questioned the police’s role in the incident. The caption of one post reads: “Alas, Bangladesh! Alas, freedom! Alas, the rule of law upheld by law enforcement!

In broad daylight, a mob is attacking a man old enough to be their father right in front of the police, yet the officers are acting like spectators, simply standing by and watching.”

item.title: Legal action if strikes called to destabilise LPG market: Energy minister
item.description:
Business owners across the country have announced that the sale of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) will be halted on Thursday and Friday.

Energy Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmud has stated that if attempts are made to create market instability through this programme, the government will take legal action.

The minister said that repeatedly attempting to raise prices by disrupting supply is unacceptable. The issues must be resolved through discussion with the business owners.

He made these comments at an impromptu press conference following a meeting with LPG operators at the Secretariat today, Thursday.

The minister mentioned that a global crisis in the energy sector has created challenges in importing and supplying LPG. Despite uncertainties around global market fluctuations and import sources, the government is trying to provide LPG to consumers at reasonable prices.

The Energy Minister stated that, due to the war situation, there is instability in the global energy sector. Private importers in Bangladesh are also having to seek alternative sources. Long-term strategies have been discussed with operators to avoid supply shortages and ensure adequate LPG supply for the upcoming year.

To stabilise supply and prices, the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has been instructed to take necessary actions, the minister said, adding that discussions are ongoing to resolve the issues faced by the business owners. Another discussion with the relevant parties will be held on 30 October.

In order to prevent the creation of artificial shortages at the dealer level, the Directorate of National Consumer Rights Protection and the district administration have been activated, the minister noted. The government will take necessary measures to keep the market situation normal.

In response to the higher LPG prices in Bangladesh compared to neighboring India, the Energy Minister mentioned that the Indian government reduces LPG prices through subsidies. Beneficiaries under specific programmes receive LPG at reduced prices there. However, such subsidies do not exist in Bangladesh, and private importers sell LPG in the open market, which affects local prices according to international market rates.

At the same conference, Commerce Minister Khandaker Abdul Muktadir stated that the government is in talks with business owners to maintain stable LPG supply and market conditions. However, creating market instability through strikes to impose demands will not be tolerated.

The Commerce Minister said that private companies import LPG. The government does not directly import LPG. Nonetheless, the BERC sets the LPG prices each month in alignment with the international market.

The Commerce Minister remarked that commercial disputes, including profits, losses, and commissions, can be resolved through discussion.

He also pointed out that the relevant authorities are prepared to listen to the business owners and solve legitimate issues. However, if anyone attempts to misuse the market system for personal gain or create situations adverse to public interest, the government will not accept it.

The LPG Business Association Cooperative Society Limited has announced a countrywide closure of LPG shops on 15 and 16 October, demanding to stop the harassment of business owners, among other issues.

The association's president, Mohammad Selim Khan, announced this decision at a press conference at the National Press Club last Monday.

He mentioned that if demands are not met, a more stringent programme may be declared following the two-day initiative.

In this situation, the government held a meeting with LPG operators today. The meeting discussed strategies for maintaining stable LPG supply now and for the upcoming year.

item.title: Description of the Declaration of Independence to change
item.description:
The National Curriculum and Textbook Board (NCTB) is introducing changes to several subjects, including history, in the textbooks for the upcoming academic year (2027). Among these changes is the description regarding the declaration of Bangladesh’s independence.

Previously, changes were also made to this topic during the tenure of the interim government. As a result, the description of the declaration of independence in textbooks now stands in three distinct versions across the tenures of the Awami League—which was ousted during the July Mass Uprising—the interim government, and the BNP (Bangladesh Nationalist Party) government.

For the upcoming academic year, approximately 310 million textbooks are being printed for students from pre-primary to class-IX, as well as for ethnic minority communities and visually impaired students. Printing is currently underway following the revisions, with a significant number of books already printed.

In the 2027 Class-VII ‘Bangladesh and Global Studies’ book, the first chapter is titled ‘Bangladesh’s Struggle for Freedom and Mass Movement’. This chapter highlights the history of Bangladesh’s struggle for liberation, culminating in the declaration of independence, the commencement of the War of Liberation, and the establishment of Bangladesh as an independent and sovereign state at the cost of the blood of three million martyrs.

Regarding the declaration of independence and the beginning of the War of Liberation, the book states, “On the midnight of 25 March 1971, the Pakistan Army cracked down on the unarmed Bengalis, unleashing a massacre. When the Rajarbagh Police Lines came under attack by Pakistani forces, news of the assault was broadcast across the country via wireless telegraph from the Police Lines base. Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was arrested that very night. The people of the country found themselves bewildered and lost amidst the leadership vacuum. Against this backdrop, upon learning of the genocide perpetrated by Pakistani forces on the night of 25 March, Major Ziaur Rahman, Second-in-Command of the 8th East Bengal Regiment, revolted in Chittagong, declaring ‘We Revolt’.

“Subsequently, at 2:15 AM (26 March), he assembled all Bengali officers and soldiers of the battalion and declared war by declaring independence. Following this declaration, the War of Liberation officially commenced. When the Swadhin Bangla Betar Kendra was established at Kalurghat in Chittagong, Major Ziaur Rahman declared the independence of Bangladesh at 6:30 pm on 27 March as the provisional President and Commander-in-Chief of the Liberation Army. Through his declaration, news of Bangladesh’s War of Liberation spread at home and abroad.

“Later, in another radio broadcast, he proclaimed independence on behalf of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman as the provisional Commander-in-Chief of the Bangladesh Liberation Army. Ziaur Rahman’s declaration of independence inspired freedom-loving Bengalis with the resolute spirit of liberty. The War of Liberation began. Ultimately, on 16 December 1971, through victory in a people’s war, 24 years of Pakistani exploitation and discrimination came to an end. At the cost of the blood of three million martyrs, Bangladesh established itself as an independent and sovereign state on the world map.”

What was written during the Interim Government

Following the fall of the Awami League in 2024, the interim government assumed responsibility and revised the textbooks and curriculum.

In the Class-VII ‘Bangladesh and Global Studies’ book prepared during that government’s tenure, the description of Bangladesh’s declaration of independence, the War of Liberation, and the attainment of victory is presented as follows, which is being taught in the current academic year.

It says, “On 25 March 1971, at midnight the Pakistan occupation military forces launched a sudden attack on the unarmed Bengalis and started a genocide. They attacked Rajarbagh Police Lines. News of the attack was telecast from the Police Lines telex message. Bangabandhu was arrested on the same night. On 26 March, Major Ziaur Rahman from the Kalurghat Radio Station of Chittagong declared the independence of Bangladesh. He then declared independence again on 27th March on behalf of Bangabandhu. The War of Liberation began. Finally, 24 years of exploitation and discrimination of Pakistanis came to an end with the victory of the people on 16th December 1971. As a result, Bangladesh emerged as an independent and sovereign country in the world in exchange of the blood of three million martyrs.”

How it was described during the Awami League Regime

During the tenure of the Awami League government, which was ousted in the July Mass Uprising, there was another version of the declaration of independence in textbooks.

The Class-VII ‘Bangladesh and Global Studies’ books for 2023 and 2024 are not available on the NCTB website. However, the description of the declaration of Bangladesh’s independence exists in the textbook from 2022 under the Awami League government.

It stated, “...On the midnight of 25 March 1971, the Pakistan Army descended upon unarmed Bengalis, unleashing a genocide. When the Rajarbagh Police Lines came under attack by Pakistani forces, news of the assault was broadcast across the country via wireless telegraph from the Police Lines base. Bangabandhu was detained that very night. Before his arrest, in the early hours of 26 March—at the midnight of 25 March—Bangabandhu declared the independence of Bangladesh. The War of Liberation began. Ultimately, on 16 December 1971, Bengalis brought an end to 24 years of Pakistani exploitation and discrimination through victory. As a result, at the cost of the blood of three million martyrs, Bangladesh established itself as an independent and sovereign state on the world map.”

Other additions and changes

In the textbooks for the upcoming academic year, historical content such as the sectors and brigade forces of the War of Liberation, biographies of the Bir Sreshthas (the highest military decorated heroes), the events of 7 November 1975, and the role of former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia in the 1990 Mass Uprising are being included. Additionally, an article authored by former President Ziaur Rahman is also being featured in the textbooks.

Apart from history, new content is being incorporated into Bengali and Information and Communication Technology (ICT). A total of four new books—two each for Class-IV and Class-VI—are being introduced. The two new books for Class-IV are ‘Culture of Bangladesh’ and ‘Sports’, while the two books for Class-VI are ‘Amar Karigoric Shikkha (vocational education)’ and ‘Anandamoy Shikkha (learning with joy)’.

Children learn differing narratives

With every change in government, the narratives surrounding several historical events, including the declaration of independence, undergo alterations. As a result, children read different accounts depending on which government is in power.

However, many contend that in the age of the internet, people now have access to a vast repository of information.

Speaking about this, Liberation War historian Afsan Chowdhury told Prothom Alo that every government alters the history of the state, and will likely continue to do so in the future.

According to him, “This is because, under the guise of studying the history of the Liberation War, political discourse takes precedence over genuine historical scholarship, driven by political self-interest. That is precisely where the problem lies.”

He further said that it must be remembered that the history of the state is not everything; social history or informal history also exists. Yet, the study of that history receives little emphasis, whereas greater importance ought to be attached to the study of social history.

item.title: Tongi drug factory fire brought under control after 4 hours
item.description:
A fire that broke out at Unit-2 of Drug International Limited in the Cherag Ali area of Tongi, Gazipur, was brought under control after nearly four hours. The fire broke out at the factory at around 10:15 am on Wednesday. As many as 21 firefighting units were working to bring the fire under control. The army and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) later joined the operation.

Director General of the Fire Service and Civil Defence Directorate, Brigadier General Sultanul Afrain Zunaid confirmed that the fire was brought under control at around 2:00 pm today.

According to Fire Service sources, the fire began around 10:15 am at Unit-2 of Drug International Limited. Within moments, the flames spread across various parts of the factory. Flames and thick smoke were seen rising from the premises. Upon receiving the report, 21 units from fire stations in Gazipur, Tongi, Uttara and surrounding areas rushed to the scene.

Senior Station Officer of Tongi Fire Service Shahin Alam said that, considering the severity of the fire, personnel from various stations conducted joint firefighting operations. The operation was challenging because the factory building was made of steel, aluminium and glass. As different parts of the building caught fire rapidly, firefighters faced difficulties bringing the fire under control.

Talha Bin Zasim, an officer at the media cell of the Fire Service and Civil Defence, said that 14 units were initially working to douse the flames. More units were subsequently dispatched to the scene, bringing the total to 21 units engaged in the operation. At one point, personnel from the Army and BGB joined the firefighting efforts.

Medicines, production machinery and other materials stored inside the factory were reportedly damaged in the fire. However, the extent of the financial damage could not be assessed immediately. No casualties have been reported so far but there is no confirmed information on whether anyone was trapped inside.

Brigadier General Sultanul Afrain Zunaid stated that the fire is suspected to have originated from chemicals stored in the factory's four-story building. Firefighters are now carrying out damping operations to extinguish the remaining flames, he said, adding that the work would continue throughout Thursday.

Necessary documents have been requested from the factory authorities and an investigation is underway to determine whether the facility had adequate fire safety measures in place, he said.

item.title: Tongi pharmaceutical factory: 20 fire service units working; Army, BGB join

A fire has broken out at a pharmaceutical manufacturing plant operated by “Drug International Limited” in the Cherag Ali area of Tongi, Gazipur.

Twenty fire service units are working to bring the blaze under control. A team from the Bangladesh Army and the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has also joined the firefighting operation.

The fire broke out at around 10:15 am on Wednesday. Shaheen Alam, senior station officer of Tongi fire service, confirmed the incident.

No casualties had been reported as of noon. However, authorities could not confirm whether anyone remained trapped inside the factory.

According to Fire Service sources, they received a report of the fire at the pharmaceutical factory in Cherag Ali at around 10:15 am.

Following the report, 20 units from various fire stations in Tongi, Gazipur, Uttara and nearby areas began working to extinguish the blaze under the leadership of Shahin Alam. Three of the units came from Tongi.

According to fire service and local sources, the fire originated in Unit 2 of the factory at around 10:15 am before spreading rapidly to other parts of the facility.

The flames and smoke subsequently intensified. Medicines, production equipment and other materials inside the factory are being damaged by the fire. However, authorities have yet to confirm which floor the fire started on.

Shaheen Alam, senior station officer of Tongi fire service, told Prothom Alo that the factory building was made of steel and aluminium and also contained glass.

“The fire is spreading rapidly because of the building’s construction materials, making it challenging for us to bring the blaze under control,” he said.

Fire breaks out at Essential Drug International in Tongi, 13 units deployed

item.title: 86 Saudi-bound flights cancelled, 13,490 passengers affected
item.description:
Restrictions at Saudi Arabia’s airports and disruptions to flight operations have severely affected Saudi-bound flights scheduled to depart from Dhaka, leaving thousands of passengers facing uncertainty.
In a statement on Wednesday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) said a total of 86 direct and transit flights had been cancelled or suspended so far, affecting 13,490 expatriates and other passengers.
Of the affected flights, 36 were direct flights and 50 were transit flights, according to CAAB.
Among airlines operating direct flights to various destinations in Saudi Arabia, 14 flights of Biman Bangladesh Airlines, 10 of US-Bangla Airlines, seven of Riyadh Airways and five of Saudia Airlines were cancelled or suspended.
Transit flights carrying passengers to Saudi Arabia via airports in the Middle East and neighbouring countries were also significantly affected. Of the 50 disrupted transit flights, IndiGo operated 22, Emirates 11, Qatar Airways and flydubai six each, SalamAir four, and EgyptAir one.
Passengers have been advised to stay in contact with their respective airlines regarding flight rescheduling or ticket date changes until the situation returns to normal.
