item.title: Saudi Arabia says Houthi attacks sparked Aramco fire, wounded 4 in Riyadh
item.description:
Saudi Arabia said on Wednesday that an attack on an Aramco building in the kingdom's east sparked a "limited fire" and that debris from intercepted Houthi missiles wounded four people in the capital Riyadh.
It came hours after the Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen's Houthis said it had intercepted several missiles on Tuesday evening, including over Riyadh.
A Saudi energy ministry official said an administrative building belonging to oil giant Aramco in Dhahran was struck on Tuesday evening, resulting in a "limited fire" but "no casualties or fatalities".
Saudi Arabia's civil defence agency said on Wednesday that four people -- two women, a man and a child -- were wounded by debris from two intercepted Houthi cruise missiles in the capital and that 15 homes were damaged.
Earlier on Tuesday, the coalition struck oil sites across western Yemen, in response to the deadliest attack on the kingdom's soil in years.
The strikes in Yemen's Sanaa and the western provinces of Dhamar and Saada targeted facilities used to "supply the war effort" by the Houthis to "threaten the kingdom, Yemen, the southern Red Sea and waterways", coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki wrote on X.
A powerful explosion then rang out in the Saudi capital, with a phone alert sent to residents saying "the city of Riyadh is facing a hostile aerial threat".
While walking down a major avenue in Riyadh, a witness told AFP he "saw a projectile cutting across the sky" above a mall, saying it left "a yellowish trail of light followed by a trail of smoke. Then, we heard an explosion".
"People were calm; no one was speaking. We were scared and all looking up at the sky," he added, requesting anonymity.
After Houthi strikes on Saudi airports and energy sites in recent days, the coalition issued its first evacuation order in the Yemeni capital since the war flared in July, before attacking the Yemen Petroleum Company facility on Sanaa's outskirts.
An AFP correspondent in Sanaa reported an explosion, while a breaking news alert on the Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah TV channel said "Saudi aggression" targeted the oil firm.
A strike on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday left 13 people dead and operations suspended in the worst attack since 2015.
The Saudi cabinet vowed in a meeting earlier Tuesday, led by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, that it "will not allow its security or freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait to be threatened".
An AFP correspondent reported that many civilians in Sanaa, fearing shortages, rushed to queue in front of fuel stations after the coalition warning.
The Houthis had earlier issued a new threat to target Riyadh's international airport, a refinery, and an Aramco facility in Dammam if the strike went ahead, calling for citizens to avoid them.
Many countries have issued travel warnings to their citizens in Saudi Arabia, most recently France, which told its citizens to avoid Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam airports.
The Saudi-led coalition has supported Yemen's government militarily against the Houthis since 2015 in a long-running civil war that has created a dire humanitarian crisis.
Traffic in perennially gridlocked Riyadh was noticeably lighter this week as remote learning for all schools and work-from-home orders for some companies took effect, according to AFP journalists.
Saudi Arabia faces a major economic contraction this year, with GDP expected to shrink 3.3 percent, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday, predicting a regional drop over Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.
The kingdom was already facing headwinds from Iran's chokehold on the Hormuz strait since the start of the Middle East war in February, when the US and Israel attacked Iran.
But the restart in July of Yemen's frozen war has further roiled the kingdom and brought the fight to its own soil.
Houthi attacks have also targeted oil tankers in the Red Sea -- Saudi Arabia's alternative export route.
In Yemen, the renewed fighting was fuelling the risk of infectious disease outbreaks.
Suspected cholera cases tripled there in three weeks, the World Health Organization said Tuesday, warning that the growing disease burden was straining hospitals already treating war casualties.
The Riyadh airport attack had prompted US President Donald Trump to say he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis.
He wrote on his Truth Social platform on Tuesday that "the Houthis are behaving very badly", accusing them of acting "probably at the behest of Iran".
"I'll be there after the elections, and I will never forget!" he wrote, referring to next month's midterms.
The Houthis warned the US against intervention, with political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti telling AFP they would target American interests in the region.
Bukhaiti said the purpose of the campaign against Saudi targets was to send a message to the crown prince "that he can no longer wage aggression against Yemen from a safe position".

item.title: Son kills mother, critically injures father in Kurigram
item.description:
A woman was killed and her husband critically injured after their son allegedly stabbed them at their home in Kurigram Sadar upazila early Wednesday.
The incident occurred around dawn in Belgachha Union, Officer-in-Charge of Kurigram Sadar Police Station Kamal Hossain confirmed the incident.
The deceased was identified as Munira Begum, 56. Her husband, Sardar Ali, 65, a retired textile engineer, sustained serious injuries and was taken to Rangpur Medical College Hospital for advanced treatment.
Their son, Mostakin Alam Shovon, 35, allegedly carried out the attack before fleeing the scene.
According to police and local residents, Shovon, who was reportedly addicted to drugs, had been sent to rehabilitation centres several times by his parents but repeatedly escaped. His parents were preparing to send him to a centre again, but he refused to go.
Staff from a rehabilitation centre in Sirajganj had arrived at the family's home early Wednesday to take Shovon to the facility.
Realising their intention, Shovon came out of his room and stabbed his mother in the chest with a knife. When his father intervened, Shovon stabbed him repeatedly in the abdomen before fleeing.
The rehabilitation centre staff rescued the injured couple and took them to Kurigram General Hospital, where the on-duty physician declared Munira dead. Ali was later referred to Rangpur Medical College Hospital for advanced treatment.

item.title: CCGP approves Tk1,466 C fertilizer imports from 4 countries
item.description:
The Cabinet Committee on Government Purchase (CCGP) on Wednesday approved the import of fertiliser worth around Tk1,466 crore from Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Russia and Canada to meet the country’s agricultural demand.
The approval was given at a meeting chaired by Finance Minister Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury.
The recommendations cover imports of urea, muriate of potash (MOP) and diammonium phosphate (DAP) fertilisers under government-to-government (G2G) agreements and existing contracts.
Under the proposals, 40,000 tons of bulk granular urea fertiliser containing 10% nitrogen will be imported from Saudi Arabia’s SABIC Agri-Nutrients Company for Tk220.65 crore. The price has been set at US$ 446.67 per ton.
The committee also recommended importing 42,000 tons of bulk granular urea fertiliser from Fertiglobe Distributions Limited of the UAE for Tk275.78 crore at $531.67 per ton.
Both urea consignments will be imported in the 2026-27 fiscal year.
The committee recommended importing 35,000 tons of MOP fertiliser from Russia’s JSC Foreign Economic Corporation (Prodintorg) for Tk166.10 crore at $383.80 per ton under a G2G agreement between the Russian company and the Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC).
It also recommended two separate imports of 40,000 tons each of MOP fertiliser from the Canadian Commercial Corporation (CCC) under G2G agreements with BADC. Each consignment will cost Tk188.90 crore, with the price fixed at $382.38 per ton.
The proposals allow for an additional 10% over the specified quantities.
In another proposal, the committee recommended importing 40,000 tons of diammonium phosphate fertiliser from Saudi Arabia’s MA’ADEN for Tk 425.58 crore under an agreement with BADC.
The DAP fertiliser will cost $861.50 per ton and forms the fifth lot of the 2026 supply arrangement.
The imports are intended to ensure the availability of fertilisers required by farmers for agricultural production.

item.title: Yamal stays cool at boiling Galatasaray to lift Barcelona to victory
item.description:
Barcelona and Lamine Yamal rediscovered their sparkle after a rocky first-half spell in the cauldron of Istanbul's Ali Sami Yen stadium to win 4-1 away to Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.
Halfway through the second round of matches, the victory lifted Barcelona to the top of the Champions League table with two wins. Galatasaray are pointless and near the foot of the standings.
"We're at a very high level. We have to keep going; the season is very long. We can't relax," Barcelona's Fermin Lopez told Spanish broadcaster Movistar.
Barcelona dominated the early stages. With Yamal vigorously policed on the right by the home defence, many of their attacks flowed through Anthony Gordon on the other flank.
Yet Galatasaray took the lead after 27 minutes. After Gordon went tumbling in the penalty box, the hosts launched a rapid counter-attack through Rafael Leao on the left.
He pulled the ball back to the edge of the area to Russian Aleksei Batrakov whose drive deflected off Joao Cancelo and into the corner of the goal.
"That goal made things a bit strange for us, because we had been dominating. But we knew how to react and come back," said Fermin.
That ignited a spell of furious home pressure which culminated with Victor Osimhen rising to head a corner past goalkeeper Joan Garcia. Baris Yilmaz toed the ball over the line but was ruled offside.
Barcelona reasserted control. When Yamal went down on the edge of the box, the ball broke to a surprised Davinson Sanchez who gave the ball away immediately. It fell to Dani Olmo who threaded a pass to Cancelo who scored.
At the start of the second half Yamal took over. After setting up Gordon, who spurned the chance, he helped put Barca ahead in the 50th minute, placing a gentle curled cross on the forehead of Fermin who nodded home.
"He's a friend and a great team-mate," said Fermin of Yamal. "When he has the ball, I always look for a run. He's the best in the world. We get along well off the field, and that shows on the pitch, too."
Three minutes later, Yamal beat Eren Elmali three times, and in three different ways, in a tiny space before rolling a pass to Gordon in front of goal.
This time the England striker made no mistake with Elmali, a Turkey international, lifting his arms to the heavens in an expression of powerlessness.
After 65 minutes Yamal cut in from his wing and fired a pass to replacement centre forward Gabriel Jesus. The ex-Arsenal man could not control the ball but it deflected to Karim Adeyemi who drilled the ball home.
And three minutes later, Yamal should have got on the scoresheet himself but after being quickest to a loose ball he fired his shot over the bar.
The 19-year-old finished the game without a goal which would have taken him closer to Kylian Mbappe's record for Champions League goals as a teenager, but Yamal, who became Barcelona's youngest ever captain in the previous round, again took over the captain's armband when Pedri was replaced.

item.title: US women rally to draw 2-2 with Spain in second friendly
item.description:
The United States salvaged a 2-2 draw with Spain on Tuesday, three days after they lost to the women's World Cup champions in a pair of home international friendlies.
Alexia Putellas and Salma Paralluelo scored five minutes apart in the first half for Spain at Subaru Park, home of Major League Soccer's Philadelphia Union.
But Ashley Sanchez pulled back a goal shortly after the break and Mallory Swanson slammed in a US equalizer in the 86th minute.
The hosts could have won it deep in stoppage time, but for a fine save from a deflected Lily Yohannes effort by Spain's goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez.
By that stage both sides had made multiple substitutions, as they build towards next year's World Cup in Brazil.
But the draw is still a major boost for the US ahead of a Concacaf quarter-final clash against El Salvador next month in which they can book their World Cup berth with victory.
Spain -- who have already qualified for the World Cup -- had beaten the US 2-0 in Washington on Saturday with goals from Patri Guijarro and Eva Navarro.
The reigning world champions were denied a fifth win in a row Tuesday since losing to England in April.
Putellas opened the scoring, tapping in from close range.
Clara Serrajordi crossed and Clara Pinedo let the ball run through her legs to two-time Ballon d'Or winner Putellas.
Paralluelo fired in Spain's second five minutes later, rattling the ball in off the crossbar after US goalkeeper Phallon Tullis-Joyce's poor clearance was intercepted.
The US struck back against the run of play in the 49th minute. Sophia Wilson raced into Spain's half but overhit her pass left to Sanchez.
She circled back toward goal, shooting from the corner of the six-yard box and into the far corner.
With four minutes of regular time remaining, Michelle Cooper collected a beautiful diagonal long ball from Kate Del Fava, miscued her initial touch but recovered to pull it back for Swanson.
Swanson flicked the ball up in the air and swiveled, drilling it into the far left corner.
Deep in injury time Spain goalkeeper Rodriguez dived low to her left to deprive Yohannes of a dramatic winner.

item.title: FIFA proposes $6.35bn soccer development fund, $25m for each association
item.description:
FIFA will propose a $6.35 billion fund for soccer development between 2027 and 2030, including an increased allocation of $25 million for each national association, according to a document reviewed by The Associated Press on Tuesday.
The world soccer governing body said the proposal aims to use the financial success of the latest World Cup to boost investment in football development across its 211 member associations, confederations and other stakeholders.
Under the previous plan, each national association was set to receive $10 million over the four-year period.
The document, dated Oct 14, said FIFA had proposed distributing more than $3.5 billion from its financial reserves, citing the unprecedented commercial success of its 48-team World Cup.
The proposal comes as European soccer leaders seek a candidate to challenge FIFA President Gianni Infantino, whose controversial plan for private investment in the World Cup was scrapped within days of its announcement in July, prompting action from UEFA.
Infantino, who took over as FIFA president in 2016, is seeking re-election next year.
The document said the financial plan would be finalised by the FIFA Council in December 2026, subject to final approval at the 77th FIFA Congress in March 2027.
FIFA also proposed allocating $99 million to each of the six continental confederations.
"If accepted, the proposal will more than double the level of planned distribution funding for the 2027-2030 period, with a specific focus on investment and development of women's and youth football," FIFA said.
In August, UEFA announced that it was preparing a criminal complaint against Infantino in Switzerland over possible financial mismanagement in the World Cup sell-off deal. It has also asked courts in the United States to authorise the discovery of evidence.
UEFA's 55 member associations account for more than a quarter of FIFA's 211 member federations eligible to vote in the presidential election scheduled for March 18 in Rabat, Morocco.

item.title: Mendis, Shanaka star in Sri Lanka consolation T20I win
item.description:
Kusal Mendis knocked a solid half century and medium pacer Dasun Shanaka grabbed three wickets as Sri Lanka beat Pakistan by eight wickets in the third and final Twenty20 international on Tuesday.
Skipper Mendis hit a 48-ball 87 with four sixes and nine boundaries as Sri Lanka chased down the 169-run target in 17.1 overs for a consolation win at Pindi Stadium.
Pakistan won the series 2-1 with four-wicket and 82-run wins in the first two encounters, also in Rawalpindi.
Pakistan, sent in to bat, were lifted to 168-8 by in-form skipper Sahibzada Farhan who scored a 47-ball 76 that included three sixes and seven boundaries.
Mendis credited disciplined bowling for the turnaround.
"We didn't bowl well in the first two games but today our bowling was disciplined and we kept them to a gettable total," said Mendis.
Farhan blamed lack of runs in the final match.
"We batted well in the first two games but this 168-run total was not enough so we have to analyse this for future games," said Farhan.
Sri Lanka started well with opener Sineth Jayawardena scoring a quickfire 26-ball 38 studded with five boundaries and two sixes.
From 74-2, Mendis and Kamindu Mendis did not let Pakistan get any more wickets, sharing an unbroken 98-run stand for the third wicket.
Kamindu struck four boundaries in his 27-ball 40 not out.
Earlier, Pakistan for the first time in the series found the going tough, losing opener Fakhar Zaman (12) and Maaz Sadaqat (nought) off successive deliveries with the score at 34.
Hasan Nawaz (16) and Abdul Samad (15) helped Farhan push the score but it was in the final five overs that Pakistan accelerated by adding 59.
The final flurry came through Arafat Minhas who helped Farhan add 66 for the seventh wicket to take the total to some respectability.
Minhas hit two boundaries and two sixes in his 20-ball 34 not out.
Besides Shanaka, Nuwan Thushara and Eshan Malinga also grabbed two wickets apiece.

item.title: Atletico sink Man Utd as Viking deny Bayern in Champions League
item.description:
Atletico Madrid beat Manchester United 2-0 in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday as the Red Devils continued their poor run, while Bayern Munich were held 3-3 in Norway by underdogs Viking Stavanger.
Elsewhere, last season's beaten finalists Arsenal eased to victory over Lille while Barcelona came from behind to beat Galatasaray but Inter Milan lost a seven-goal thriller at home to Club Brugge.
Atletico, who lost at Liverpool in their opening European encounter, took the lead inside the opening minute in the Spanish capital through Pablo Barrios. Alejandro Grimaldo struck the woodwork from a free-kick later in the first half.
Johnny Cardoso also had a goal disallowed before the break but Ademola Lookman got Atletico's second in the 79th minute, just after United defender Leny Yoro had been sent off.
The defeat continued the Old Trafford club's disappointing start to the campaign and increased the pressure on manager Michael Carrick.
They have gone five matches without a victory and have won only once in seven outings, with a trip to Italy to face Como next up in the Champions League.
"Tonight is a one-off game in judgement, it is the Champions League and a tough place to come. We are doing certain things OK," Carrick told broadcaster Amazon Prime.
Viking, who are in the Champions League after winning a first Norwegian title in 34 years, appeared to be heading for a famous win over Bayern when they led 2-0 at half-time in Stavanger.
Gianni Stensness headed them in front in the second minute and Peter Christiansen ran away to double their advantage.
Harry Kane pulled one back from a penalty early in the second half and then headed in his eighth goal of the season in nine games in all competitions.
Luis Diaz then converted as the match was turned completely on its head, but Bayern's Michael Olise was sent off in the 74th minute -- the France star was booked and then shown a second yellow seconds later for throwing the ball at his opponent.
He will therefore miss next week's home meeting with Arsenal.
Viking snatched a memorable draw as Herman Haugen headed home in the last minute.
Speaking to Amazon Prime, Kane said Olise "will be gutted and he has to take responsibility for it. It was a mistake, and mistakes happen. He has to learn from it. It's a shame because we have important games ahead of us."
Arsenal were too strong for Lille as the Premier League champions won 3-0 at the Emirates Stadium with goals by Jurrien Timber, Eberechi Eze and Bukayo Saka, in the space of eight second-half minutes.
Barcelona, one of the favourites to win the competition, maintained their 100 per cent record this season with a 4-1 win over Galatasaray in Istanbul.
Russian international Aleksei Batrakov gave the Turkish champions the lead and they then had another goal disallowed, but Joao Cancelo equalised before half-time.
Lamine Yamal then turned on the style, setting up goals for Fermin Lopez and Anthony Gordon early in the second half, before substitute Karim Adeyemi sealed Barca's victory.
Italy-born German striker Nicolo Tresoldi scored a hat-trick, including a penalty, as Club Brugge claimed a remarkable 4-3 win away to Inter at San Siro.
Romeo Vermant got the Belgians' other goal, with Lautaro Martinez on target twice for Inter as they succumbed to a second straight European defeat.
In other games, Villarreal came from behind to beat Napoli 3-1 in Spain while RB Leipzig beat PSV Eindhoven 1-0 with a Brajan Gruda goal after Ivan Perisic failed to convert a penalty for the Dutch side.
Sporting of Portugal won 2-0 away to Lens in France with goals by Luis Suarez and Issa Doumbia, and it was a night to remember for Sabah as the rank outsiders from Azerbaijan downed Slavia Prague 2-0 in Baku.
Jamaican international Kaheem Parris and Rwanda's Joy-Lance Mickels secured their first victory in the league phase.
Wednesday's Champions League games include reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain at Manchester City and Real Madrid at Roma.
